key_insight: ANTIC uses a neural, in-situ compressor that adapts compression fidelity over time to dramatically reduce storage for high-resolution, spatiotemporal PDE simulations while preserving scientifically relevant features.
problem_solved: Massive storage and I/O bottlenecks from petabyte-to-exabyte scale transient simulations (e.g., Navier–Stokes, MHD, plasma, black-hole mergers) that make long, high-resolution runs and post-hoc analysis impractical.
method: Neural latent-space compression (e.g., autoencoder-style model) trained or tuned to represent high-dimensional PDE fields compactly.
Adaptive temporal allocation: dynamically vary compression fidelity/bitrate across time steps to focus capacity on periods of complex dynamics.
In-situ integration with HPC simulation loops and error-aware reconstruction controls to meet scientific error tolerances while minimizing I/O.
impact: Enables orders-of-magnitude reduction in storage and I/O for large-scale simulations, making long-term, high-fidelity runs and downstream ML/analysis feasible on existing HPC resources.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing simulation → in‑situ ANTIC compressor → compressed archive → reconstruction/analysis.
Temporal fidelity chart: variable bitrate over time highlighting high-complexity windows preserved at higher fidelity.
Before/after field snapshots or difference heatmap to show preserved features and reconstruction error.
Storage vs. error trade-off curve comparing ANTIC to standard compression and fixed-rate neural compressors.
paper_title: ANTIC: Adaptive Neural Temporal In-situ Compressor
paper_authors: Sandeep S. Cranganore, Andrei Bodnar, Gianluca Galleti, Fabian Paischer, Johannes Brandstetter
